paragraphs: In one sentence: an art director does not just make one attractive image but turns a business or narrative goal into a visual direction that many people can execute consistently and that can be approved and delivered. The US side corresponds to O*NET-SOC 27-1011.00; the BLS 2025 wages shown on O*NET are a median annual wage of 114,850 US dollars (10th percentile 64,900, 90th percentile 213,050), and the 2024—2034 employment growth shown on O*NET is average (3% to 4%). This round's NBS release does not provide a nationwide wage for this occupation, and this page uses only industry category average wages as background.

Editorial trial: use the complete fictional inputs provided in the path section for the "Paper Light Culture Festival" to complete a 90-minute direction board, two sketch options, a review, and v2 change records. Observe whether the audience, fixed copy, color constraints, and to-be-confirmed status can be stated clearly; this is not merely a comparison of which final image looks better, nor a hiring test.

Reasons to pause before paying for expensive training: you have not yet completed one small end-to-end project from brief, direction, and feedback to final artwork, or you can show only final images without being able to explain why things were cut or changed; and you have not yet verified the basic requirements for copyright and licensing, delivery specifications, and the approval chain.

Education, certificates, licenses, job hiring, institutional authorization, and signing responsibility must be verified separately: a bachelor's degree and related experience are a common path for most positions in this occupation, but the portfolio and a reviewable delivery process explain ability better than certificates; entry thresholds are set by the specific employer and project requirements, and this page provides no institution's hiring standards.

In one sentence: this is an occupation whose core duties are setting visual direction, directing artwork and layout output, organizing multi-disciplinary reviews, and finalizing within budget, time, and media specifications. Whether one is competent depends on the portfolio, the delivery process, and collaboration performance, not personality labels. US wages and employment have official figures (2025 median annual wage 114,850 US dollars; 2024—2034 average growth 3% to 4%), while Chinese wage data this time consists only of broad industry background.

The work of art directors falls into four categories: setting visual direction (reading the product, brand, or narrative brief, determining the concept, references, color, typography, photography, or illustration direction, and giving executable rules); organizing and reviewing output (assigning tasks, reviewing intermediate drafts, resolving cross-media inconsistencies, and approving artwork and prepress proofs); communicating with clients and decision-makers (determining goals, budget, background, and presentation method with the client, presenting the final layout and obtaining approval, and recording conclusions and the scope of changes); and management and delivery (managing one's own clients and projects, working within budget and schedule requirements, agreeing the scope of services with printers and production partners, and keeping version and delivery records). All four categories require stating the direction clearly, explaining the trade-offs, and making output reviewable within authorization and rights boundaries. The O*NET tasks also include drawing illustrations, setting type, and designing game interfaces; art directors may perform these personally, and direction responsibility and specific production cannot be divided into mutually exclusive occupations.

Data basis: US occupational code 27-1011.00; the O*NET Job Zone Four describes relatively high preparation requirements, and AE describes the interest environment; this round's NBS release has no dedicated art director wage, and industry averages serve only as background.

Insufficient evidence: this round's 2025 NBS release does not provide the art director occupational median, starting salary, or city ranking. Culture, sports, and entertainment 129,447 non-private and 64,015 private yuan/year are only broad industry pre-tax averages and cannot be used to infer individual wages.

O*NET-SOC 27-1011.00 Art Directors. Official skills and knowledge profile: the core skills are active listening (75) and speaking (75), critical thinking (69) and reading comprehension (69), writing (60) and active learning (56); transferable skills rate judgment and decision making (69), complex problem solving (66), coordination (66), and time management (66) as high, with persuasion (60) and operations analysis (60) next. The official duty is "formulate design concepts and presentation approaches for visual communications media, such as print, broadcasting, video, and film, and direct workers engaged in artwork or layout design." O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed, SVP 7.0 to below 8.0), and the generic note for that zone states that most occupations in the zone require a four-year bachelor's degree, which is not the educational share of all positions in this occupation. The BLS description for this occupation is usually a bachelor's degree and related experience.

The comparison is of main outputs: graphic design emphasizes specific visual communication; set and exhibition design emphasizes space; digital interfaces emphasize interface usability; game design emphasizes gameplay systems; producing and directing emphasize overall production; craft art emphasizes physical creation; and project management emphasizes scope and schedule. Duties may overlap, and art directors may also set type, draw, and manage budgets; legal discretion and client confirmation are not obtained automatically from a job title.

The objects are the visual concept and direction, material details such as layout and graphics and imagery and sound, and the artwork and prepress materials produced by the team; the basis is the brief and brand or narrative goals, media specifications and delivery standards, budget and schedule, and material rights and approval requirements.

Measured by whether the direction supports the objective, whether the output meets specifications and is brand-consistent, whether rights and sources are clear, whether the approval chain and versions are complete, and whether delivery is on schedule, not by the look of a single final image or proficiency in a single tool.

The brief and direction boards, reference and material source records, review comments and decision-maker records, versions and the finalization package, material licenses and authorization credentials, and the pre-check list and delivery acceptance records.

Visual direction, specific design, and budget and scheduling may be carried by the same person. Before starting, state who reviews, who commits the budget, and who confirms delivery; divide work by the specific project authorization, and refer difficult rights questions to the corresponding responsible person.

Work must follow the contract and project requirements: material use complies with copyright and the scope of the license; where portraits or minors are involved, verify the required consent by jurisdiction and use; on-site shooting and equipment work comply with safety rules; delivery files are organized per the specification and naming and version requirements; and when rights or safety boundaries are unclear, verify before acting.

When material sources or authorization are unclear, specifications conflict with brand requirements, the approval chain is missing, or on-site and personnel safety risks arise, stop the affected steps, keep the original records and versions, and ask for instructions and escalate through the project decision chain, and do not skip rights verification or alter approval records because of a delivery deadline.

Portfolio and case conclusions apply only to specific project objectives, media specifications, and team conditions; the same direction may differ in effectiveness across media and audiences, a single project's success must not be presented as a general rule, and past project experience must not be treated as acceptance evidence for a new project.

Before starting, verify at least six items: occupational scope (US side O*NET 27-1011.00, and the Chinese position title and duty boundaries must be verified against actual duties); education and portfolio requirements (most positions require a bachelor's degree and related experience, and the evaluation focuses on direction building, review, and the delivery process); the scope of decision and acceptance authority (which directions the person decides and which must be approved by the client or brand); rights and compliance requirements (material licenses, portrait and minor consent, and source records and archiving); the form of work and compensation method (employment, freelance, or per-project pay affects income stability and working hours); and tool and delivery specification requirements (industry-common tools and media specifications, which vary considerably across teams).
Look at the position duties and decision authority first, then the job title.

entries.answer: The official duties are to formulate design concepts and presentation plans for visual works and media such as print, broadcast, video and film, and to direct staff engaged in art creation or layout design. Daily work includes reading the brief and setting layout or presentation, specifying details of materials such as typefaces, photographs, graphics, animation, video and sound, assigning tasks and reviewing intermediate drafts and prepress proofs, agreeing goals and budget with clients and presenting the final layout, managing own clients and projects and working within budget and schedule requirements. The 16 O*NET tasks also cover consulting creative, copy and production leads, reviewing whether art materials meet standards, agreeing the scope of services with printers and estimators, attending shoots and print sites, and researching current trends and new technologies.
entries.question: What does an art director do every day?

entries.answer: Graphic designers deliver concrete layouts and visual products; set and exhibition designers deliver spatial schemes; web and digital interface designers deliver interfaces and interaction specifications; video game designers deliver gameplay and systems design; producers and directors take creative and production responsibility for the complete programme; craft artists produce handcrafted works; project management specialists and IT project managers manage scope, schedule and resources. The core of art direction is setting visual direction, organising and reviewing output and being responsible for consistency, and the responsibility boundary and qualification requirements cannot be swapped with those of other directions.

subject.summary: Art directors (O*NET-SOC 27-1011.00, Art Directors) formulate design concepts and presentation approaches for visual works and media such as print, broadcast, video, and film, and direct staff engaged in artwork or layout design. This page verifies the official duties and tasks, wages and employment, industry and tool signals, rights and risk boundaries, and data gaps: the US side has official wage and employment figures (May 2025 median annual wage 114,850 US dollars; BLS 2025—2035 employment growth 4%), while Chinese wage data this time consists only of broad industry background, and this page labels them separately.
